questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Create a habit of checking your safety belt and making sure all passengers buckle theirs before you start driving.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To change lanes safely, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far or as clearly in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far or as clearly in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of passengers.
You can only turn in certain directions from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes must merge carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of passengers.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. It is reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
A winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your driver license and registration ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to come to you.
Get out of your car and walk to the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to come to you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Remain in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its red stop arm out, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait before driving.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left side.
Keep driving once you think the children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before it opens its door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait before driving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with its red stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not drive until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: You can help someone hurt in a crash by:

options.text: Calling for medical help.
Putting pressure on or bandaging wounds.
Arranging a ride to the hospital.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers in a crash should help injured people. This means calling for medical help, arranging transportation, or putting pressure on or bandaging any bleeding wounds.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: An intersection is ahead.
A steep hill is ahead.
A winding road is ahead.
Traffic is merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downhill grade ahead.

questions.question: In a construction zone, be ready to:

options.text: Stop.
Change lanes.
React to workers or equipment moving suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In construction zones, be ready to slow down or stop for workers and equipment. Be ready to change lanes. Watch for sudden movement from workers or equipment.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Recognize that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not follow this driver's example.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Stay focused on the road. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space. Distracted drivers are more likely to cause accidents.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other alcohol
Illegal drugs and prescription medicines
Inhalants such as glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road will cross a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads with a median or guard rail between them.

questions.question: One of your tires blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Steer straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control of the car. Then brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When is texting while driving allowed?

options.text: When there are very few cars around.
Never.
If you use voice-to-text.
If you only look away for a few seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to read, write, or send text messages while driving. Do not answer calls or respond to texts while driving. Violating this law will result in fines.

questions.question: An aggressive driver cuts you off. What should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Take your own aggressive action to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Do not try to get even. This only makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all cars are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how to operate it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how to operate it.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes learning the location and use of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce it. These may help you stay awake, but they will not make you sober or lower your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What happens if you leave the scene of an accident with injuries or death?

options.text: Jail only.
A fine only.
Jail and a fine.
No punishment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Jail and a fine.
questions.explanation: If you are in an accident that injures or kills someone, you must stop right away and stay at the scene. If you leave, you may face jail time and fines. You must return to the scene immediately if you did not stop.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on a highway. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Get back at the other driver by cutting them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: Do not take aggressive action when another driver cuts you off. Stay calm and continue driving safely to avoid road rage situations.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with no traffic signs or signals at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and get through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Slow down and let them pass before you proceed.

questions.question: When an aggressive driver is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Retaliate by tailgating them.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down, let them pass, and do not make eye contact or make gestures.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: Following too closely means you may not have enough time to stop and avoid a collision if the car ahead suddenly slows or stops.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Proceed normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when near a blind pedestrian. Give them the right-of-way and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Inattentive driving
Excessive speed for the driving conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: All three are major causes of accidents. Driving too fast, not paying attention, and tailgating are common reasons for crashes.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When may drivers leave their vehicle unattended with the engine running?

options.text: If they are leaving for just a couple minutes.
Never.
If they are idling near a railroad crossing.
If they are idling in an unfamiliar area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to leave a car running and unattended. You must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the brake. Remote starters that start the engine without the key in the ignition are the only exception.

questions.question: When you see a warning sign, what should drivers do?

options.text: Pay attention to their surroundings.
Follow instructions.
Reduce their speed to the posted advisory speed.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about conditions ahead. Pay attention to your surroundings, follow the sign's instructions, and reduce speed if recommended.
